why: Deviation D-11 makes the pinned cornerstone3D 5.8.2 the definition of correct for this project, because HLD section 11 makes it the reference the oracle measures against and decision D7 makes the oracle the thing that exists before port code. So a place where the pin is wrong about PS3.3 has to be written down here, or a pixel diff measures our correct arithmetic against its incorrect arithmetic and reports the difference as ours. Decision D14 publishes a MEASURED divergence, which is a number with a side attached, and this file is what attaches the side. A new entry is a reviewed change with a rationale, exactly as a tolerance change is: this register is the one mechanism in the comparator that can turn a failure into a non-failure, so it gets the same handling as the other one.
strictness: Strict in the direction that can be true today. An entry marked reachable false that FIRES is a run failure, because the claim was wrong. The opposite direction, an entry no row exercises failing the run, is unsupported.json's other half and is NOT applied here: the only entry is unreachable by today's corpus and applying it would fail every run from the first one. That asymmetry is decision 12 of F-011's design round and docs/lld/comparator.md records it.
matchLanguage: Each entry's `match` object maps an RFC 6901 pointer into the REFERENCE side's sidecar to exactly one test. The tests are `equals`, `lessThan` and `greaterThan`, and every condition must hold for the entry to fire. A test this comparator cannot evaluate is REFUSED at load rather than read as unsatisfied, because a condition nobody evaluates is an entry that never fires and nobody notices.

entries.reachableWhy: All eighty-five windowed corpus rows resolve LINEAR, so no view reaches this. It is written down because the first SIGMOID row added to the corpus will meet it. Resolving the case itself is F-X012, S04. F-011 built the register that holds it.
entries.referenceDoes: cornerstone3D 5.8.2's utilities.windowLevel.toLowHighRange applies LINEAR's (w - 1) / 2 to SAMPLED_SIGMOID as well as to LINEAR, so a width between 0 and 1 produces an INVERTED range: width 0.5 at centre 40 gives lower 39.75 and upper 39.25.
entries.standardRequires: C.11.2.1.3.1 gives SIGMOID as y = (ymax - ymin) / (1 + exp(-4 * (x - c) / w)) + ymin, which divides by w and therefore requires only w > 0. C.11.2.1.2 requires w >= 1 for LINEAR because LINEAR divides by w - 1. The minimum width is per function and not shared, and the difference between the two is a half and a one.
entries.pixelEffect: An inverted window maps the display range backwards over the affected stored values, so the frame is inverted across the window rather than differing by a code or two. It is a whole-frame effect on any row that reaches it and not a rounding difference.
